geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Measure before and after; test k < 1 and k > 1.

Goal: I can verify that a dilation maps a line not through the center to a parallel line, leaves a line through the center unchanged, and multiplies every segment length by k.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
For k > 0, a dilation preserves angles and multiplies every segment length by k. A line through O maps onto itself. A line not through O maps onto itself when k = 1 and onto a distinct parallel line when k ≠ 1. If O, A and B are collinear, A′ and B′ remain on that line and A′B′ = k AB.

Postulate (assumed here, not proved by proportional sides): these dilation properties are assumed here. The Side-Splitter Theorem in 8.6 uses these explicit assumptions; measuring in the sandbox is not a proof.

Drag center and k; segments and their images update with ratios, including a line through the center that maps to itself.

Use the controls in the panel. Drag the hollow points on the board.
